_comment: #256 Phase B, second rig (added after the tournament-caps corpus grew to include a physically different rig alongside Calling Edinburgh). Measured against 3 imported full-broadcast Pro Tour Las Vegas captures (all 2048px-wide after import normalization): sourceFile 'Screenshot 2026-08-04 at 16.22.59.png' (imported as 70295169f6953958.png, 2048x1150), 'Screenshot 2026-08-04 at 16.23.18.png' (4a00635d5c50dacf.png, 2048x1156), and 'Screenshot 2026-08-04 at 16.24.40.png' (306e65a7849abd2b.png, 2048x1146). Measured via the SAME direct pixel-color sampling method as calling-edinburgh.json (chrome banner/gold-art colors vs. the mat's flat teal tone). Play-area-adjacent boundaries: top edge 0.058-0.061, left edge 0.193-0.195, right edge 0.806-0.811 -- ALL within ~1% of calling-edinburgh.json's own measured numbers (0.057-0.061 / 0.196-0.197 / 0.803-0.809), confirming the two rigs share the same underlying broadcast-production template (camera framing, chrome proportions) and differ only in mat color and chrome branding art -- not a coincidence, a real structural commonality worth noting, not assumed. The webcam/info-stack/card-preview sub-splits within each sidebar reuse calling-edinburgh.json's own proportions (visually confirmed matching layout in the measured captures: player webcam + rig-branding logo upper sidebar, TCGPLAYER sponsor block + tournament round/turn/clock info stack lower-left, real rendered card lower-right) -- same secondary, lower-stakes caveat as calling-edinburgh.json's own _comment (the rigorously measured boundary is chrome-vs-play-area, not the further sub-split).
name: Pro Tour Las Vegas broadcast rig (landscape table, two players seated left/right, overhead camera, teal/gold mat with gold-and-green chrome and TCGplayer sponsor blocks -- distinct from calling-edinburgh.json's white/lavender mat and blue chrome, same underlying production template) -- geometry measured against imported real captures under pipeline/out/backgrounds/captures/, see this file's _comment for exactly which ones and how; the captures themselves are never committed (copyrighted broadcast footage, see importCaptures.ts).
